sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
I am happy you are here.
Today we will talk about Ghana.
Ghana is a warm, colorful, and friendly country in West Africa.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Ghana?
Ghana is in West Africa.
It is next to Cote d'Ivoire, Burkina Faso, and Togo.
To the south, it touches the Atlantic Ocean.
This part is called the Gulf of Guinea.
Ghana has beaches, forests, lakes, and cities.
What is the capital city of Ghana?
The capital city is Accra.
Accra is on the coast.
It has markets, museums, traffic, and modern buildings.
Other important cities are Kumasi, known for culture and history,
tamale in the north,
Takarati and Cape Coast with beaches and forts.
How many people live in Ghana?
About 34 million people live in Ghana.
Ghana has many ethnic groups and local languages.
It is one of the most peaceful and stable countries in Africa.
What language do people speak in Ghana?
The official language is English.
It is used in schools, government, and media.
Many people also speak local languages,
such as Tuayu Dagbanigafante.
People often speak more than one language.
What is the weather like in Ghana?
Ghana has a tropical climate.
It is usually hot and humid.
There are two main seasons.
Rainy season with heavy rain and green landscapes.
Dry season, hot and sunny,
sometimes dusty,
harmant and winds.
People wear light clothes and drink lots of water.
What does Ghana look like?
Ghana has coastlines and beaches.
Forests like the Kacum National Park.
Savannah is in the north.
Lakes like Lake Volta, one of the biggest in the world.
It is a country full of natural beauty and wildlife.
What animals live in Ghana?
You can see monkeys, antelope, and elephants.
Crocodiles, lizards, and turtles.
Birds like parrots and eagles.
Goats, sheep, chickens, and cows on farms.
Some people visit national parks to see wild animals.
What do people eat in Ghana?
Ghanaian food is spicy, rich, and filling.
People eat rice, yam, plantain, and cassava.
Fish, chicken, and goat meat, vegetables, and sauces.
Popular dishes, jalaf rice,
spicy rice with tomato and meat.
Bufu softo made from cassava or yam eaten with soup.
Vancouver fermented corn dough with fish,
kelewelli, spicy fried plantains.
Waki rice and beans.
People often eat with their hands,
especially in traditional meals.
What do people drink in Ghana?
People drink water and coconut water.
Fruit juices, like mango or pineapple.
Soft drinks, herbal drinks.
Adults may drink pito or palm wine.
Coconut sellers are common on the streets, fresh and cold.
What is life like in Ghana?
Life in Ghana is full of energy, community, and music.
People enjoy spending time with family,
talking to neighbors, going to church or mosque,
dancing and listening to music,
watching football, the national sport.
Markets are busy and full of color, sound, and smells.
What are some holidays and traditions in Ghana?
Independence Day, March 6,
Republic Day, July Friend,
Hummelville Festival in Acra with music and food,
Abokir Festival, a hunting tradition,
Christmas, Edal feeder, and Edal ada.
People celebrate with drums,
dancing, special clothes, and family meals.
Some fun facts about Ghana.
Ghana was the first African country to gain independence
from colonial rule in 1957.
The Ghanaian flag is red, yellow, green,
with a black star.
Ghana is known for kente cloth, colorful and hand woven.
The national football team is called the black stars.
Ghana produces gold, cocoa,
and music loved around the world.
Now you know many things about Ghana.
You know where it is, what people speak,
and what they eat.
You learned about the weather, culture, music, and life.
Well done.
I am Emily.
Goodbye.
Or as they say in tweet, not to ye.
